notes: SMALLEST HONEST CHANGE: a declared table from situation key to tendency, read where `tendencyOrder[0]` is read today, and no proposal at all where the table has no entry. That is C11's fourth case — an optional observation is omitted rather than invented. Nothing else needs building. What a player would see: a proposed change that is about what actually kept happening to them, and no proposal after situations that bear on nothing.

PLAYER-FACING INPUT: yes, and it is the whole point. A development proposal is shown to the player and requires their choice (`requiresPlayerChoice: true`). So the player is currently being asked to accept or refuse a change about risk-taking on the evidence of two lunch-table choices.

Related to the thresholds review's disposition on personality evidence: two copies of one event are one observation. That half is now fixed — occasions are counted rather than rows — and is a separate matter from which tendency the occasions bear on.

WHAT THE SCHEMA HOLDS TODAY, because a disposition that names a record is only actionable if the record exists: the situation-to-tendency table does not exist anywhere. There is no field for it on a tendency definition, none on a situation definition, and no separate record. So this is a schema-and-content job, not a reclassification. What a save loses if the recommended answer is taken and the table starts empty: nothing a player would miss, because today's proposals are all the same one — but it is worth saying rather than discovering, since the surface does go quiet until the table is filled.
question: For each of the twenty formative situations the game can put to a player, which personality tendency does repeating it bear on — and which of them bear on none, so that repeating them should propose no change at all?

title: Which part of a person each formative situation actually bears on
usableAnswer: A row per situation naming the tendency it bears on, or naming none explicitly. "None" is a real answer and the more useful one where it is true: a situation that bears on nothing should propose nothing rather than propose something arbitrary. Where a situation plausibly bears on a tendency the catalog does not carry, say which tendency is missing rather than forcing it onto one of the six.
whyItMatters:
Measured at main `1c4992e8`: when two distinct occasions of the same formative situation occur between the player and the same person, `character-history.ts` proposes a character development. The tendency it proposes is `mindCatalog.tendencyOrder[0]` — the catalog's first entry, every time, whatever those occasions were about. In the synthetic catalog that is `riskApproach`, so **every character development the game has ever proposed, in every life, has been about risk approach**, including after two lunch-table choices or two conflicts with a friend. The evidence decides whether a development is proposed and has no influence whatever on which one. This is the sharpest instance yet of the pattern the owner named after his ten-year run — a producer that runs, reads its evidence, and then ignores it. The repeated-count half is fixed; this half cannot be fixed without an authored link, and inventing twenty mappings is content this lane will not make up.

The twenty situations: activity-choice, belief-challenge, broken-object, care-conflict, caring-for-someone, civic-volunteering, friend-conflict, future-preparation, household, household-transition, illness-in-the-house, lunch-table, money-shortfall, school-entry, school-rule-input, small-money, student-organizing, teacher-mentor, teen-work-opportunity, workplace-rule.

The six tendencies available: riskApproach, responseTempo, conflictApproach, curiosity, loyalty, ambition.

candidateAnswers.label: Silence where nothing is borne on
candidateAnswers.position: Map only the situations that genuinely bear on one of the six tendencies, and have a situation with no entry propose nothing at all. A proposal is never made on a default, a nearest match or the catalog's first entry.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: A development proposal is shown to the player and asks them to accept or refuse it. Asking someone to decide about a change to their risk-taking on the evidence of two lunch-table choices is not a wrong mapping, it is the game asking a question it has no business asking. Silence is the honest output when the link is unknown, and it is the same rule the missing-fact classification already sets for an optional observation: omit it or state its absence, never invent a value. It also degrades safely as the catalog grows, because a newly added situation proposes nothing until somebody says what it bears on.
candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: Fewer proposals reach the player than today, and on the twenty situations as they stand it may be a lot fewer. Today's proposals are all the same one, so nothing true is lost, but the surface does get quieter until the table is filled in.

candidateAnswers.label: Map all twenty, nearest fit
candidateAnswers.position: Assign every one of the twenty situations to whichever of the six tendencies it comes closest to, so a proposal always follows repeated history.
candidateAnswers.argumentFor: Keeps the frequency of proposals roughly as it is, and no situation is left inert.
candidateAnswers.argumentAgainst: Several of the twenty do not plausibly bear on any of the six — a household transition or starting school is not obviously about risk, tempo, conflict, curiosity, loyalty or ambition. Forcing a nearest fit reproduces the present defect in a politer form: the player is still asked about a change the evidence does not support, and now with a mapping table that makes it look considered.

answer.summary:
## A02 — Formative experience must affect what actually happened

**Question:** `which-tendency-a-formative-situation-bears-on`.

The current source still proposes development after sufficient interaction records by taking `mindCatalog.tendencyOrder[0]`. Catalog ordering is not evidence. Replace that default with the supplied semantic/context table and preserve the newer independent-occasion safeguards.

The correct mapping depends on the **chosen option and its reason**, not just the scene title. Accepting a job, declining it to protect an existing obligation, and waiting for more information are different decisions. None universally establishes risk-taking. A household change does not specify a trait at all.

The table accounts for every requested name. It uses the exact stored keys where relevant: `risk-approach`, `response-tempo`, `conflict-approach`, `curiosity`, `loyalty-tendency`, and `ambition`, not the request's informal camel-case labels. Conditional links propose evidence, not a compulsory trait change. Missing more specific facets such as honesty, responsibility or assertiveness are named rather than forced into “risk.”

Some examples:

- An actual inquiry about unfamiliar work can support curiosity or waiting for context. It is not proof of academic skill.
- Saying one disagrees can be evidence of accepting direct confrontation in that exchange; it neither changes the underlying belief nor proves hostility.
- Protecting either family care or a prior outside promise may reflect loyalty. Need the actual bond and the chosen reason; the option alone does not decide.
- Admitting responsibility for a broken object concerns truthfulness and responsibility. Silence does not automatically prove a deliberate lie.
- Joining or leaving an activity first affects participation, time, interests and goals. The personality conclusion requires an actual pattern and motivation.

### Two adjacent source defects to remove from the same pathway

The current resolver marks withdrawn-option choices as a mixed appraisal and applies fourteen days of “formative tension.” That makes a reasonable boundary or choosing not to argue feel wrong by construction. Make emotional consequences depend on the actual appraisal instead.

Several current memory strings assert later outcomes immediately: a mediation “fixed it,” outside help “eventually worked,” and a chosen job “stayed yours for years.” A selection cannot establish those unexecuted facts. Record the action or intention now, and describe the result when the corresponding existing continuation actually reaches it. The same episode identity should connect those stages.

**Acceptance:** reordering tendency definitions never changes a life's interpretation; no trait proposal from a scene without evidence; actual choices differ; duplicates are not independent experience; inner choices are not known to bystanders; a narrative cannot commit an unperformed outcome. The bare `household` request needs its actual producer/key before that one row can be implemented.
